newsitem.title: MEXICO: Tax payments fall sharply in Mexican city of Leon.
newsitem.headline: Tax payments fall sharply in Mexican city of Leon.

text.p: The payment of federal taxes in the north-central city of Leon has fallen by 40 percent this year because of a shortage of liquidity among taxpayers and because of the complexity of tax laws, the Leon College of Public Accountants said on Monday.
"The problem is a lack of money among business people," said Juan Abel Cardiel, president of the accountants group. "Either they meet the payroll and pay creditors or they pay taxes."
Abel Cardiel criticized the tax code established by the Finance Ministry, saying that each time it is supposed to be simplified it comes out more complicated.
"We are convinced that when the tax system is easier to understand, both for accountants as well as for business owners, collecting taxes will be a lot easier," he said.
Abel Cardiel called on accountants nationwide to pressure for a simpler tax code, but he doubted progress would be made because of mid-term elections set for next year.
